title: Sustainability pillar (minimize environmental impact)
hook: The Sustainability pillar asks you to minimize the environmental impact of running cloud workloads — understand your footprint, maximize utilization, and choose efficient architectures and regions.

blocks.text: Principles: understand impact, establish sustainability goals, maximize utilization, anticipate and adopt efficient offerings, reduce downstream impact, and measure. Practices: right-size, Graviton (ARM) instances, serverless for variable load, S3 lifecycle to colder tiers, delete unused resources, and consider carbon footprint of regions (Customer Carbon Footprint Tool).

blocks.text: Enterprise RFPs increasingly ask for carbon reporting. Sustainability overlaps Cost and Performance — efficient architecture is often cheaper. Interviewers test whether you know it is the sixth pillar, not an afterthought.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: maximize utilization, efficient instance types, serverless, lifecycle policies, measure with Carbon Footprint Tool.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Measure footprint
items.body: Customer Carbon Footprint Tool; correlate with Cost Explorer.

items.title: Maximize utilization
items.body: Right-size, auto scale in, schedule dev environment shutdown.

items.title: Choose efficient services
items.body: Graviton, serverless, managed services over idle VMs.

items.title: Reduce data waste
items.body: Lifecycle policies, compress logs, delete unused snapshots.

diagram.title: Sustainability levers
diagram.source:
flowchart TB
  MEAS[Carbon Footprint Tool] --> UTIL[Right-size / scale in]

  EFF --> DATA[S3 lifecycle / log retention]

snippet.label: Carbon footprint report
snippet.code:
aws bcm-data-exports create-export \
  --export DataExportName=carbon-footprint \
  --data-query '{"QueryStatement":"SELECT * FROM carbon_footprint"}'

snippet.label: S3 lifecycle to IA
snippet.code:
LifecycleConfiguration:
  Rules:
    - Id: transition-logs
      Status: Enabled
      Prefix: logs/
      Transitions:
        - StorageClass: STANDARD_IA
          TransitionInDays: 30
        - StorageClass: GLACIER
          TransitionInDays: 90
snippet.explanation: Colder tiers reduce storage energy footprint and cost.

snippet.label: Graviton ECS task
snippet.code:
TaskDefinition:
  Properties:
    Cpu: 512
    Memory: 1024
    RuntimePlatform:
      CpuArchitecture: ARM64
    ContainerDefinitions:
      - Name: api
        Image: myapi:arm64
snippet.explanation: Graviton delivers better performance per watt for many workloads.

snippet.label: Schedule dev shutdown
snippet.explanation: Zero utilization overnight — sustainability and cost win.

rows: No cloud carbon equivalent in typical Node hosting

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: Oversized instances running 24/7 at 10% CPU. Never expiring logs in S3. Ignoring Sustainability pillar entirely in WAFR.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: carbon report trend quarter-over-quarter; Graviton adoption %; average CPU utilization; S3 storage class distribution.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: Saying sustainability does not apply to cloud — rejected. Strong answer: maximize utilization, efficient hardware, lifecycle, measure footprint.

interviewTakeaways: Sustainability = minimize environmental impact via utilization and efficient architecture.
Often aligns with Cost and Performance — not separate effort.
Graviton, serverless, lifecycle policies are primary levers.
60s: Measure with Carbon Footprint Tool. Right-size, Graviton, serverless, S3 lifecycle, delete waste. Sixth pillar — enterprise customers ask.
Follow-up: how does region choice affect carbon footprint?
commonPitfalls: Ignoring sixth pillar — looks uninformed in enterprise interviews.
Strong answer: utilization, Graviton, lifecycle, measurement tool.
Infinite log retention without business need.
